requirement_text.REQ-066: Port src/api/errors.zig (272 lines) and src/api/response.zig (69) as Letflow.Api.Error and Letflow.Api.Response -- the single response/error contract every S4 route emits. Nothing in this batch renders a response body by hand once these exist. errors.zig is an RFC 9457 Problem Details builder. Port: the ProblemDetails shape (type as an absolute URI under a configured base, title, status, detail, plus the trace id field errors.zig carries with a "" default), the per-status constructors (problemNotFound and its siblings for 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/500 -- enumerate them from the Zig source rather than guessing which exist), and serialisation to a JSON body. Emit Content-Type: application/problem+json on error responses, per RFC 9457, and state in the moduledoc whether R-Co does the same or emits application/json (check response.zig's CONTENT_TYPE_JSON usage) -- if Letflow diverges, that divergence is deliberate and documented, not accidental. response.zig defines the canonical HandlerResult (status_code, body, content_type defaulting to JSON) and the typed success constructors that keep positive responses on correct status codes (200 vs 201 vs 202 vs 204). In Elixir the conn IS the result carrier, so port these as functions that take and return a conn (send_json/3, created/2, no_content/1, and the error counterparts) rather than transliterating a HandlerResult struct -- Zig returns a value because it has no conn. State that translation in the moduledoc. SECURITY (INV-4, INV-5): an error body must never carry secret material, a raw Ecto/Postgrex error, or a stack trace -- detail is a caller-safe string chosen by the handler, and an unexpected internal error maps to a generic 500 problem document whose detail does not vary with the underlying exception. Separately, the not-found problem document is the exact response a cross-tenant probe receives (REQ-072 enforces the routing; this requirement guarantees the two bodies are byte-identical by construction, because both go through one constructor).

You FAILed this gate at commit 8807851 with three items and stated the re-review scope on resubmission is narrow: the router catch-all, the four router_test.exs assertions, and send_problem/2's trace_id -- everything else already signed off as-is. ITEM REVIEWER-02d-1: lib/letflow/router.ex's catch-all reportedly now calls Letflow.Api.Response.not_found(conn). Confirm no hand-built error body remains anywhere in the router, and confirm the private send_json/3 delegate is still correct for GET /health.

Do NOT re-litigate: main's pre-existing repo-wide mix format and --warnings-as-errors failures, already filed as docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml / GH#354 / queue task 170. Confirm only that this run's own files introduce no new warning or formatting failure.

result.summary: PASS. All three rework items independently re-derived from the code at HEAD 5e4f7f5; ELIXIR-DEV's report was not relied on. Gate is clear, TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3) may start. ITEM REVIEWER-02d-1 -- router catch-all: PASS. lib/letflow/router.ex:27-29 is now `match _ do Letflow.Api.Response.not_found(conn) end`. Grepped the whole file: no map literal, no Jason.encode!, no send_resp, no put_resp_content_type remains anywhere in router.ex -- the only two body-producing sites are the /health success and the catch-all, and both now go through Letflow.Api.Response. The hand-built %{error: "not_found"} document is gone, so the system no longer ships two structurally different 404s, and the 404 the catch-all emits is byte-identical to any other Response.not_found/1 by construction (single Error.not_found/0 constructor, no varying input) -- which is exactly what REQ-072's cross-tenant-probe guarantee will lean on. The private send_json/3 delegate was kept rather than inlined (my FAIL said either was fine); it is still correct for GET /health: Response.send_json/3 is put_resp_content_type("application/json") + Jason.encode! + send_resp at the given status, identical to the behaviour the old private function had, and the router test asserts 200 + %{"status" => "ok"} and passes. It now has exactly one call site, which is a style nit, not a defect -- the explaining comment above it makes the delegation deliberate. ITEM REVIEWER-02d-1b -- router_test.exs assertions: PASS, and the body check got strictly STRONGER, not weaker. The @not_found_body module attribute at test/letflow/router_test.exs:36-42 spells out all five RFC 9457 fields literally (type/title/status/detail/trace_id). I verified each field against the constructor rather than against the attribute: type = @problems_base <> "not-found" where @problems_base is Application.compile_env(:letflow, :problems_base_uri, "https://bpm.example.com/problems/") and nothing in config/*.exs sets :problems_base_uri (grepped all five config files -- zero hits), so the compile-time value is the default and the literal "https://bpm.example.com/problems/not-found" is correct; title "Not Found"; status 404; detail = @not_found_detail = "the requested resource was not found"; trace_id "" because nothing in lib/ assigns conn.assigns[:trace_id] (grepped -- the only trace_id hits outside error.ex/response.ex are in engine/plugin_interface.ex, an unrelated plugin-context field). The old assertion pinned a 1-key map; the new one pins a 5-key map with the exact base URI, so a silent drift in the wire contract that the old assertion would have passed through now fails four tests. Spelling the document out literally instead of calling Error.not_found/0 is the right call and I explicitly endorse it: deriving the expected body from the constructor under test would make the assertion tautological and unable to catch a contract change at all. All four 404 tests (POST /instances, POST /instances/:id/actions, GET /instances/:id, arbitrary unknown route) still assert BOTH conn.status == 404 AND full body equality -- verified line by line at 59/60, 71/72, 80/81, 87/88. The REQ-046 regression intent survives intact: the status assertion is what carries it (a pre-REQ-046 router would have raised UndefinedFunctionError and 500ed rather than reaching a clean 404), the moduledoc paragraph explaining that intent for cases 2-4 is untouched, and no test name or describe block changed at all -- the diff touches only the new attribute and the four right-hand sides -- so docs/anti-patterns.md's ExUnit 255-char combined describe+test name entry is not engaged (longest name here is 45 chars, and there are no describe blocks in this file). Ran the file: `mix test test/letflow/router_test.exs` -> "Finished in 0.08 seconds ... Result: 5 passed", 0 failures. ITEM REVIEWER-02d-2 -- send_problem/2 trace_id: PASS. ELIXIR-DEV chose FIX over document, which is the better of the two options I offered. Verified against the R-Co source directly, not against the report: c:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/R-Co/src/api/errors.zig line 54 reads `const effective_trace_id = if (p.trace_id.len > 0) p.trace_id else trace_context.get();`, and the ProblemDetails field doc at lines 30-37 states the same three-step precedence plus 'setting it explicitly overrides the thread-local (useful in tests)'. lib/letflow/api/response.ex:179-180 implements `defp effective_trace_id("", conn), do: conn.assigns[:trace_id] || ""` / `defp effective_trace_id(trace_id, _conn) when is_binary(trace_id), do: trace_id`. Elixir has no zero-length-binary state other than "", so the first clause is exactly Zig's `p.trace_id.len == 0` branch and the second is exactly `p.trace_id.len > 0` -- the precedence matches 1:1 in all three cases: non-empty document trace_id wins, else conn.assigns[:trace_id] (Letflow's conn-scoped stand-in for the trace_context thread-local, per stage-4-api-surface.md's 'do not port a thread-local global'), else "". The caller-set-trace_id discard and the blanking-to-"" that my FAIL flagged are both gone. The moduledoc on send_problem/2 was rewritten to state the three-step precedence and to name it as matching errors.zig's serialise/2, so the divergence I objected to no longer exists and no fourth translation note is needed. INV-4 BACK-DOOR ANALYSIS (the specific concern raised on this re-gate). The new defp is NOT a back door, and SECURITY-REVIEWER's INV-4 argument survives intact -- though its EVIDENCE phrasing ('neither module defines a single defp') is now stale and should not be re-quoted verbatim in later gates; the substance of the argument never depended on the absence of a defp, it depended on the absence of a PARAMETER through which exception-derived text can reach a body. Four reasons this helper cannot become one: (1) SCOPE -- effective_trace_id/2 reads and returns only the trace_id field. It cannot touch detail, type, title or status; those four are still fixed inside their constructors in error.ex and are untouched by this rework. The INV-4 claim is about `detail` on a 500 body, and no code path from this helper reaches `detail`. (2) UNREACHABILITY for the two invariant-bearing helpers -- Response.internal_error/1 calls Error.internal() and Response.not_found/1 calls Error.not_found(); both constructors take no argument and neither sets trace_id, so both inherit defstruct's `trace_id: ""` default. Clause 1 therefore ALWAYS fires for those two, meaning their behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was before this rework. INV-4's generic-500 guarantee and INV-5's byte-identical-404 guarantee are both unaffected. (3) NO NEW CAPABILITY -- clause 2 is reachable only by a caller that hand-builds %Error{trace_id: <text>} and calls send_problem/2 directly. Any caller that can do that can already pass arbitrary text as `detail` to eight of the ten constructors, so the helper grants nothing a hostile-or-careless caller did not already have; it is the same trusted-handler boundary INV-4 already draws ('detail is a caller-safe string chosen by the handler'). And it is the behaviour R-Co documents as supported. (4) THE ASSIGNS PATH IS UNCHANGED -- clause 1's `conn.assigns[:trace_id] || ""` is character-for-character the expression that was already there pre-rework and that SECURITY-REVIEWER passed; nothing in lib/ writes that assign today, so it is dead until a trace-id plug lands. Conclusion: the helper narrows nothing and widens nothing on the INV-4 surface. WARNINGS AND FORMATTING (ISS-0106 not re-litigated): `mix format --check-formatted lib/letflow/api/response.ex lib/letflow/router.ex test/letflow/router_test.exs` exits 0. `mix compile --force` grepped for response.ex / router.ex / api/error.ex produces zero hits -- no warning attributable to this run's files. The warnings that do appear (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:879-881 JoinCounter type warnings) are pre-existing on main and are ISS-0106/GH#354's toolchain-pin problem. No new warning, no new formatting failure. NOTHING ELSE RE-OPENED: per my stated re-review scope, items (2) constructor split, (3) pattern-copy + Jason.Encoder, and (4) decision-0001/no-Phoenix consistency remain signed off from the first pass and were not revisited. NON-BLOCKING NOTES (recorded, no action this run): (a) effective_trace_id/2 has no clause for a non-binary trace_id -- %Error{trace_id: nil} would raise FunctionClauseError rather than silently coercing. Given @type t declares trace_id: String.t() and every constructor defaults it to "", this is unreachable through the public API, and failing loudly is the better failure mode than emitting a malformed body; noted only so a future Error-building path knows the field is binary-only. (b) router.ex's private send_json/3 now has a single call site (/health). Harmless, and the comment above it records why the delegation was kept; if a later S4 requirement adds success routes it will earn its keep, otherwise a future run may inline it. (c) My earlier notes stand unchanged: @problems_base is compile-time (fine, matches errors.zig's `const BASE`, but a per-tenant problem URI would need a deliberate move to runtime config), and lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex's reject_migrating/1 still builds its own response inline -- now the ONLY remaining place in the codebase reaching around the shared response contract, worth picking up in REQ-070/REQ-071.
